title: Continuous telemetry can enable linkage of the wearer's activities across time and contexts
description: The flow sends rich sensor telemetry including heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps from the wearer to the wearable device. The combination of precise location and time with behavioral and physiological signals can act as a quasi-identifier, allowing records from different sessions or contexts to be linked to the same individual.
assumptions: The wearable stores or otherwise maintains per-user/per-device association across repeated measurements, or the data is later combined with other records.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is based on general LINDDUN linkage concepts; the exact sub-node id is inferred rather than retrieved from the provided context.

title: Sensor telemetry directly identifies or singles out the wearer
description: GPS trajectories, timestamps, and biometric/behavioral telemetry collected continuously from the user can identify or single out the wearer, even if no explicit name is included in this particular flow. Home/work locations and unique movement or physiology patterns may reveal identity.
assumptions: Telemetry is associated with a persistent device, account, or recurring observation window sufficient to single out one person.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree sub-node id is inferred from standard identifiability concepts and may not match a specific repository node.

title: The flow discloses sensitive personal information to the device beyond what the user may expect
description: Heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps reveal health, habits, movement patterns, routines, and possibly visits to sensitive locations. Continuous collection increases the amount and granularity of disclosed information, creating a privacy threat if the device obtains more sensitive detail than necessary for the intended function.
assumptions: The wearable has access to raw or fine-grained telemetry and the data are available for processing, storage, or onward transfer.
uncertainty_note: Generic disclosure node used because the supplied context did not include a more specific disclosure subtree.

title: The wearer may be unaware that continuous use shares personal data with the device
description: By merely wearing the device, the user continuously provides personal data to the wearable process. The wearer may not fully understand the scope, frequency, precision, or categories of telemetry being captured, especially the combination of GPS position and timestamps with physiological data.
assumptions: Collection begins automatically during normal wear and transparency/notice may be limited or not salient at the moment of capture.

title: Continuous collection of telemetry may be non-compliant with data minimization or valid-consent requirements
description: Capturing heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps continuously may exceed what is necessary for a specific purpose, or may occur without sufficiently specific, informed, and freely given consent. This creates a non-compliance risk for principles such as purpose limitation, data minimization, transparency, and lawful basis.
assumptions: Not all listed telemetry elements are strictly necessary at all times for the intended service, or consent and notices are not granular enough.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree node id is inferred from common non-compliance branches; repository-specific node numbering may differ.

title: Companion app may receive more personal data than necessary during sync
description: The wearable sync includes exercise sessions, GPS traces, device identifier, and timestamps. Transferring full GPS traces and stable device identifiers to the companion app may constitute avoidable disclosure if the app only needs summaries or coarse location for its features. This flow should be assessed for data minimization and whether all fields are necessary at sync time.
assumptions: The app can provide some user-facing functionality without always requiring raw GPS traces or a persistent device identifier for every sync.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement for explicit disclosure / excessive collection; retrieved context confirms Dd applies to Process->Process flows but does not provide the exact subtree citation.

title: Synced sensor batches enable identification of the user through direct and quasi-identifiers
description: Even if the wearable account name is absent from this flow, stable device id combined with detailed exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps can identify or single out a person. Home/work locations and habitual movement patterns are particularly identifying, making the receiving app a point where identity can be inferred from the data payload.
assumptions: The device identifier is stable across syncs and GPS traces are sufficiently precise to reveal recurring locations.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is inferred from general LINDDUN identification threats; retrieved context only establishes that I applies on Process->Process flows.

title: Cross-session linkage is possible via persistent device id and recurring trace patterns
description: A persistent device id and repeated timestamped GPS/activity batches allow the companion app to link multiple sync events to the same individual over time. Even if some records were pseudonymous, recurring route patterns and temporal signatures can connect them into a longitudinal profile.

title: Detailed activity and location history enables profiling of sensitive habits
description: The combination of exercise sessions, fine-grained GPS traces, timestamps, and device-level continuity allows the companion app to infer behavioral patterns such as home/work, routines, health and fitness habits, religious or political attendance, and social relationships. This creates a detectability/inference risk beyond the explicit content of individual records.

description: If the wearable synchronizes detailed location trails, timestamps, and a stable device identifier without sufficiently specific notice or choice, the data flow may conflict with the user's expectations and any consent previously obtained. The privacy risk lies in the transfer being broader or more granular than what the user reasonably understands from device setup or app onboarding.
assumptions: User notices or consent dialogs may describe activity syncing at a higher level without clearly stating raw location-trace transfer and identifier use.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on actual notice/consent UX, which is not provided. Included because this flow contains sensitive, granular data whose transfer often exceeds user expectations if not clearly disclosed.

description: Calorie intake, meal descriptions, and weight entries can allow the app or its operators to infer additional sensitive information about the wearer, such as dieting behavior, eating habits, health conditions, pregnancy, or religious/cultural practices, beyond what the user may expect from the manual entry itself.

title: Disclosure of highly sensitive nutrition and body-weight data to the app
description: This flow sends intimate personal data from the wearer to the companion app. If the app collects more detail than strictly necessary, or if transmissions are accessible to unauthorized parties inside the app ecosystem, the wearer’s dietary habits and weight data may be exposed.
assumptions: The mobile app or backend receives and can access the logged values; protections and minimization may be incomplete.

title: User may be unaware of how manual diet and weight entries will be used or shared

Precise, timestamped location history is highly sensitive personal data and can reveal home/work addresses, routines, visits, and other intimate patterns. If the app stores more precision, frequency, or history duration than strictly necessary for the feature, the flow causes avoidable disclosure through over-collection and over-storage.

title: Location history entries may be alterable without preserving correctness and provenance
description: When the app writes GPS traces to the store, absent integrity protections an attacker, compromised component, or buggy client could modify timestamps or coordinates, insert false visits, or delete segments. Because location history may drive user-facing timelines, inferences, or safety-relevant features, incorrect stored data can directly harm the data subject's privacy interests and downstream decisions.
assumptions: Assumes no strong write validation, tamper evidence, or provenance controls are in place on writes to the location history store.
uncertainty_note: Exact integrity subtree node is chosen by best judgement; applicability depends on whether the store enforces authenticated, validated writes.

title: Users may be unaware that precise timestamped location traces are being persisted
description: This write flow persists detailed GPS history to storage. If the app interface does not clearly signal that continuous or repeated locations are stored, for how long, and for which purposes, users may misunderstand the system's behavior and cannot form an accurate mental model of the privacy impact.

title: Storing location history may exceed or diverge from the user's consent or expected purpose
